glossary.definition: Hand gesture of protection, fearlessness, and divine reassurance. The right hand is held upright with palm facing outward and fingers pointing upward.
A tripartite standing body curvature where the head, torso, and legs bend in opposing diagonal angles, imparting extraordinary fluidity and rhythm to sculpted divine and feminine figures.

A mythological composite beast possessing the body of a lion, head of an elephant, and tail of a serpent or peacock. Revered as an auspicious protector and frequent motif on Vijayanagara and Dravidian pillars.
A celestial maiden or bracket sculpture depicted breaking or touching a blossoming branch of a Sala tree, symbolizing tree-worship, fertility, and auspicious feminine beauty.
The sanctum tower erected directly over the Garbhagriha (inner sanctum) in Dravidian temple architecture, typically stepped and crowned with a domical Shikhara.
The superstructure or curvilinear mountain-like tower rising above the sanctum in Nagara architecture, evoking the cosmic axis and sacred Mount Meru.
The demon dwarf personifying spiritual ignorance, egoism, and heedlessness, depicted being pinned down beneath Lord Shiva Nataraja's right foot.
The halo or aureole of fiery cosmic flames encircling divine figures (especially Chola bronze Natarajas), signifying the boundless cosmos and the dance of energy.
Sacred attributes, emblems, or weapons held by deities (such as the Trishula, Chakra, Shankha, Damaru, or Gada) symbolizing cosmic faculties and divine governance.
Monumental, ornate entrance tower crowning the gateways into South Indian Dravidian temple enclosures, often adorned with multi-tiered polychrome or granite sculptures.

educationalInstitutions.name: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)
educationalInstitutions.role: Premier government organization responsible for archaeological research, conservation, and protection of over 3,690 monuments of national importance.

educationalInstitutions.name: National Museum, New Delhi
educationalInstitutions.role: Premier national repository holding world-famous collections of Indus Valley, Maurya, Gupta, Chola, and Pallava sculptures.

educationalInstitutions.name: Government Museum, Egmore (Chennai)
educationalInstitutions.role: Celebrated worldwide for having the largest and finest collection of original Pallava and Imperial Chola bronze masterpieces.

educationalInstitutions.name: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA)
educationalInstitutions.role: Autonomous trust under the Ministry of Culture dedicated to research, documentation, and dissemination of Indian arts and Silpa Sastras.
